chapters.title: Variables
chapters.summary: A variable is a storage location for holding a value . The set of permissible values is determined by the variable's type .

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: Modules are how Go manages dependencies.

chapters.title: Modules, packages, and versions
chapters.summary: A module is a collection of packages that are released, versioned, and distributed together. Modules may be downloaded directly from version control repositories or from module proxy servers.

chapters.title: go.mod files

chapters.title: Minimal version selection (MVS)
chapters.summary: Go uses an algorithm called Minimal version selection (MVS) to select a set of module versions to use when building packages. MVS is described in detail in Minimal Version Selection by Russ Cox.

chapters.title: Workspaces
chapters.summary: A workspace is a collection of modules on disk that are used as the main modules when running minimal version selection (MVS) .

chapters.title: Compatibility with non-module repositories
chapters.summary: To ensure a smooth transition from GOPATH to modules, the go command can download and build packages in module-aware mode from repositories that have not migrated to modules by adding a go.mod file .

chapters.summary: The module cache is the directory where the go command stores downloaded module files. The module cache is distinct from the build cache, which contains compiled packages and other build artifacts.
